ASSAM_CULTURE.name: Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu)
ASSAM_CULTURE.about: The Assamese New Year — drum, dance and the gamosa, celebrated for seven days across the state.

ASSAM_CULTURE.name: Kati Bihu
ASSAM_CULTURE.about: A quiet observance during the growing season, with lamps lit near the tulsi plant and in paddy fields as prayers for the crop.

ASSAM_CULTURE.name: Magh Bihu
ASSAM_CULTURE.about: The harvest-season celebration known for community feasts, traditional foods and the meji bonfire.

ASSAM_CULTURE.name: Sattriya
ASSAM_CULTURE.about: A classical dance tradition developed in Assam's Vaishnavite sattras and associated with Srimanta Sankardev and Madhavdev.

ASSAM_CULTURE.name: Borgeet & Kirtan
ASSAM_CULTURE.about: The devotional songs of Sankardev and Madhavdeva sung at naamghars and sattras across Assam.

ASSAM_CULTURE.name: Ali-Ai-Ligang
ASSAM_CULTURE.about: The Mising spring festival that marks the beginning of sowing, celebrated with dance, music and community gatherings.

ASSAM_CULTURE.name: Dogri — the Karbi festival
ASSAM_CULTURE.about: The new-year celebration of the Karbi folk with the bwenkavil and the rhythmic drum beat.

ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.name: Muga silk
ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.about: The rare gold silk of Assam, a GI-tagged treasure woven in Titabar and Nahoripathar.

ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.name: Eri silk
ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.about: The 'peace silk' of the hills — warm, creamy and used for mekhela-samel and rington.

ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.name: Pat silk
ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.about: Fine glossy silk from the Brahmaputra banks, worn in the Bihu and wedding ceremonies.

ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.name: Gamosa & Jaapi
ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.about: The white-red gamosa of honour and the conical jaapi hat — symbols of Assamese grace.

ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.name: Bell metal (Kahor)
ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.about: The hammered bell-metal of Assamese kitchens and sattra refectories, handed down for generations.

ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.name: Bamboo & cane
ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.about: Baskets, mats and furniture woven from the bamboo of the forests — daily craft of the villages.

ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.name: Terra-cotta & masks
ASSAM_HANDICRAFTS.about: Terracotta horses of Garhislal and the masks of Majuli, worn in the Bhaona dance-drama.

ASSAM_HERITAGE.name: The Ahom kingdom
ASSAM_HERITAGE.about: The Ahom dynasty ruled Assam for six centuries; a kingdom of the Brahmaputra's heartland.

ASSAM_HERITAGE.name: Srimanta Sankardev
ASSAM_HERITAGE.about: The 15th-century saint, poet and playwright who brought Vaishnavism, Sattriya and the naamghosha.

ASSAM_HERITAGE.name: The sattras of Majuli
ASSAM_HERITAGE.about: Monastic homes of the Brahmaputra islands, where Sattriya and ritual music still live.

ASSAM_HERITAGE.name: Kamakhya Devi
ASSAM_HERITAGE.about: The temple of Kamakhya atop Nilachal Hill, one of the oldest Shakti shrines of India.

ASSAM_HERITAGE.name: Sivasagar
ASSAM_HERITAGE.about: Seat of the Ahom kings — Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar, Joysagar tank and the Shiva dol.

ASSAM_HERITAGE.name: Hajo & Sualkuchi
ASSAM_HERITAGE.about: The holy town of Hajo where faiths meet, and Sualkuchi, the muga-silk village on the Brahmaputra.
